goal: Activate one shared, immutable 80-slot Raider.IO player set behind the existing talent and equipment simulator contracts, with one importable talent template per class/spec/Hero and two distinct importable equipment templates per class/spec.
userValue: A player can choose any specialization, import the two real Hero-player equipment templates, switch to either Hero tree and import the matching real-player talent template, while talent and gear remain visibly attributable to the same snapshot.
nonGoals: No BiS optimizer, recommendation scoring, DPS ranking or scheduled combat SimulationCraft.
No WCL election, anonymous fallback, baseline substitution, cross-Hero fill or cross-specialization fill.
No frontend winner election, LKG policy, pairing logic or read-time source synchronization.
No retail pointer activation or production timer cutover before candidate proof and explicit WeChat acceptance.

mustChange: Collect and seal exactly 80 class/spec/Hero/scenario slots from the established Raider.IO source, with two distinct identities per specialization.
Compile talent and gear atomically against current local authorities and reuse unchanged projections rather than rebuilding the whole release chain.
Retain the same slot's last-known-good talent and gear together when a new player cannot map, while allowing other slots to update.
Serve the active TemplateSet through the existing talent, gear and exact import APIs with shared projection, snapshot and source identity provenance.
Run one bounded scheduled Registry sync and expose read-only 80-slot health without changing retail before acceptance.
mustNotChange: Canonical Talent Catalog, Gear Release, Resolver and serializer remain the mapping and legality authorities.
The active Taro pages retain their current import controls and do not acquire data-election responsibilities.
The existing retail Manifest, retail observed-build pointer and public production route remain unchanged during candidate verification.
riskUnknown: Raider.IO may not currently yield two distinct fully mappable Hero players for every specialization within the bounded collector budget.
A dependency revision drift during collection requires controlled cutover and must not auto-promote.
An exact observed profile may expose an item variant that the current Gear Release cannot resolve, requiring same-slot LKG or explicit pending state.
evidenceRequired: Local observed-build, store, read-model, import, frontend and full Harness verification at a clean task head.
PostgreSQL backup, additive migration, exact candidate commit/tree and isolated backend on 127.0.0.1:18787.
Candidate-only real Raider.IO collection with 80 verified slots, 40 distinct player pairs and an unchanged retail pointer.
Exhaustive 80 talent reads/imports, 40 gear reads, 80 gear imports and 80 talent/gear identity matches.
Candidate pointer rollback and restore, timer/backflow state, bounded health and real WeChat DevTools acceptance.

ownership.factOwner: ObservedBuildSnapshot owns captured player facts; Projection Compiler owns current local mapping; TemplateSet owns 80-slot LKG and publication; PostgreSQL pointer owns atomic candidate or retail activation.

engineeringHealth.reason: This changes PG-backed public readers, exact imports, health, scheduled synchronization and two active WeChat user paths. Candidate migration, controlled source collection, exhaustive imports, rollback and manual acceptance are required.

acceptanceEvidence: Strict Harness full profile at a clean exact task head.
Candidate-only PostgreSQL migration, real source collection, 80-slot API/import audit and pointer rollback proof.
Official WeChat DevTools opened against the isolated candidate backend through a local SSH tunnel.
Explicit user acceptance of every frozen manual item before merge or retail activation.

decisionLog.decision: Talent and equipment simulation share the same 80 real Raider.IO player slots: 40 specializations times two Hero trees.
A verified new player may switch automatically when dependencies are unchanged; an unmappable replacement keeps the exact slot's previous talent and gear together as stale LKG.
The user approved one controlled Raider.IO collection and asked to continue through a WeChat DevTools-verifiable candidate without expanding beyond the core path.
